definition.text: Enables the transmembrane transfer of an ion by a channel that opens when a specific extracellular ligand has been bound by the channel complex or one of its constituent parts.
A membrane raft that is part of the plasma membrane.

Enables the facilitated diffusion of a monoatomic ion (by an energy-independent process) by passage through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel without evidence for a carrier-mediated mechanism. May be either selective (it enables passage of a specific ion only) or non-selective (it enables passage of two or more ions of same charge but different size).
Binding to acetylcholine, an acetic acid ester of the organic base choline that functions as a neurotransmitter, released at the synapses of parasympathetic nerves and at neuromuscular junctions.
The change in morphology and behavior of a mature or immature B cell resulting from exposure to a mitogen, cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or an antigen for which it is specific.

The process in which the anatomical structure of the optic nerve is generated and organized. The sensory optic nerve originates from the bipolar cells of the retina and conducts visual information to the brainstem. The optic nerve exits the back of the eye in the orbit, enters the optic canal, and enters the central nervous system at the optic chiasm (crossing) where the nerve fibers become the optic tract just prior to entering the hindbrain.
Any process that activates or increases the frequency, rate or extent of the regulated release of dopamine.

The process whose specific outcome is the progression of the vestibulocochlear nerve over time, from its formation to the mature structure. This sensory nerve innervates the membranous labyrinth of the inner ear. The vestibular branch innervates the vestibular apparatus that senses head position changes relative to gravity. The auditory branch innervates the cochlear duct, which is connected to the three bony ossicles which transduce sound waves into fluid movement in the cochlea.

A specialized area of membrane of the axon terminal that faces the plasma membrane of the neuron or muscle fiber with which the axon terminal establishes a synaptic junction; many synaptic junctions exhibit structural presynaptic characteristics, such as conical, electron-dense internal protrusions, that distinguish it from the remainder of the axon plasma membrane.

results.name: regulation of circadian sleep/wake cycle, REM sleep

definition.text: Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep.

The directed movement of a monoatomic ion into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore. Monatomic ions (also called simple ions) are ions consisting of exactly one atom.
The directed movement of calcium (Ca) ions into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of an acetylcholine stimulus.

The membrane component of the postsynaptic specialization. This is the region of the postsynaptic membrane in which the population of neurotransmitter receptors involved in synaptic transmission are concentrated.

The part of synaptic transmission occurring in the post-synapse: a signal transduction pathway consisting of neurotransmitter receptor activation and its effects on postsynaptic membrane potential and the ionic composition of the postsynaptic cytosol.

definition.text: A process in which force is generated within smooth muscle tissue, resulting in a change in muscle geometry. Force generation involves a chemo-mechanical energy conversion step that is carried out by the actin/myosin complex activity, which generates force through ATP hydrolysis. Smooth muscle differs from striated muscle in the much higher actin/myosin ratio, the absence of conspicuous sarcomeres and the ability to contract to a much smaller fraction of its resting length.

results.name: social behavior

definition.text: Behavior directed towards society, or taking place between members of the same species. Occurs predominantly, or only, in individuals that are part of a group.

results.comment: Behavior such as predation which involves members of different species is not social. Communication between members of different species is also not social behavior.

results.name: transmembrane signaling receptor activity

definition.text: Combining with an extracellular or intracellular signal and transmitting the signal from one side of the membrane to the other to initiate a change in cell activity or state as part of signal transduction.

results.comment: This term includes intracellular membrane receptors, e.g. IP3 triggered release of Ca2+ from intracellular stores.

definition.text: A specialized area of membrane on either the presynaptic or the postsynaptic side of a synapse, the junction between a nerve fiber of one neuron and another neuron or muscle fiber or glial cell.

The junction between an axon of one neuron and a dendrite of another neuron, a muscle fiber or a glial cell. As the axon approaches the synapse it enlarges into a specialized structure, the presynaptic terminal bouton, which contains mitochondria and synaptic vesicles. At the tip of the terminal bouton is the presynaptic membrane; facing it, and separated from it by a minute cleft (the synaptic cleft) is a specialized area of membrane on the receiving cell, known as the postsynaptic membrane. In response to the arrival of nerve impulses, the presynaptic terminal bouton secretes molecules of neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. These diffuse across the cleft and transmit the signal to the postsynaptic membrane.

A specialized area of membrane facing the presynaptic membrane on the tip of the nerve ending and separated from it by a minute cleft (the synaptic cleft). Neurotransmitters cross the synaptic cleft and transmit the signal to the postsynaptic membrane.

The progression of the lateral geniculate nucleus over time from its initial formation until its mature state. The lateral geniculate nucleus is the primary processor of visual information received from the retina.

Any process that stops, prevents, or reduces the frequency, rate or extent of action potential creation, propagation or termination. This typically occurs via modulation of the activity or expression of voltage-gated ion channels.

results.name: central nervous system projection neuron axonogenesis

definition.text: Generation of a long process of a CNS neuron, that carries efferent (outgoing) action potentials from the cell body towards target cells in a different central nervous system region.

results.name: response to hypoxia

definition.text: Any process that results in a change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a stimulus indicating lowered oxygen tension. results.name: signal transduction

definition.text: The cellular process in which a signal is conveyed to trigger a change in the activity or state of a cell. Signal transduction begins with reception of a signal (e.g. a ligand binding to a receptor or receptor activation by a stimulus such as light), or for signal transduction in the absence of ligand, signal-withdrawal or the activity of a constitutively active receptor. Signal transduction ends with regulation of a downstream cellular process, e.g. regulation of transcription or regulation of a metabolic process. Signal transduction covers signaling from receptors located on the surface of the cell and signaling via molecules located within the cell. For signaling between cells, signal transduction is restricted to events at and within the receiving cell.

results.comment: Note that signal transduction is defined broadly to include a ligand interacting with a receptor, downstream signaling steps and a response being triggered. A change in form of the signal in every step is not necessary. Note that in many cases the end of this process is regulation of the initiation of transcription. Note that specific transcription factors may be annotated to this term, but core/general transcription machinery such as RNA polymerase should not.

definition.text: The series of molecular signals generated as a consequence of an acetylcholine receptor binding to one of its physiological ligands.
Any process in an organism in which a relatively long-lasting adaptive behavioral change occurs as the result of experience.

The activities involved in the mental information processing system that receives (registers), modifies, stores, and retrieves informational stimuli. The main stages involved in the formation and retrieval of memory are encoding (processing of received information by acquisition), storage (building a permanent record of received information as a result of consolidation) and retrieval (calling back the stored information and use it in a suitable way to execute a given task).

The series of events required for an organism to receive an auditory stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Sonic stimuli are detected in the form of vibrations and are processed to form a sound.

The series of events required for an organism to receive a visual stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. Visual stimuli are detected in the form of photons and are processed to form an image.

The specific movement from place to place of an organism in response to external or internal stimuli. Locomotion of a whole organism in a manner dependent upon some combination of that organism's internal state and external conditions.

results.name: neurotransmitter secretion

definition.text: The regulated release of neurotransmitter from the presynapse into the synaptic cleft via calcium-regulated exocytosis during synaptic transmission.

results.comment: A neurotransmitter is any of a group of substances that are released on excitation from the axon terminal of a presynaptic neuron of the central or peripheral nervous system and travel across the synaptic cleft to either excite or inhibit the target cell. Among the many substances that have the properties of a neurotransmitter are acetylcholine, noradrenaline, adrenaline, dopamine, glycine, gamma-aminobutyrate, glutamic acid, substance P, enkephalins, endorphins and serotonin.

definition.text: The series of events required for an organism to receive a painful stimulus, convert it to a molecular signal, and recognize and characterize the signal. A painful stimulus is any physical or chemical event that has the potential to cause tissue damage (actual or perceived) and activates the nociceptive system.
The leaflet of the plasma membrane that faces the extracellular side of the cell, including any protein embedded in, attached to, or peripherally associated with it.

The vesicular release of acetylcholine from a presynapse, across a chemical synapse, the subsequent activation of dopamine receptors at the postsynapse of a target cell (neuron, muscle, or secretory cell) and the effects of this activation on the postsynaptic membrane potential and ionic composition of the postsynaptic cytosol. This process encompasses both spontaneous and evoked release of neurotransmitter and all parts of synaptic vesicle exocytosis. Evoked transmission starts with the arrival of an action potential at the presynapse.

Any process that modulates the frequency, rate or extent of dopaminergic synaptic transmission, the process of communication from a neuron to another neuron across a synapse using the neurotransmitter dopamine.
The change in morphology and behavior of a mature or immature B cell resulting from exposure to a mitogen, cytokine, chemokine, cellular ligand, or an antigen for which it is specific.

name: CHRNB2
comment: FUNCTION Component of neuronal acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) that function as pentameric, ligand-gated cation channels with high calcium permeability among other activities. nAChRs are excitatory neurotrasnmitter receptors formed by a collection of nAChR subunits known to mediate synaptic transmission in the nervous system and the neuromuscular junction. Each nAchR subunit confers differential attributes to channel properties, including activation, deactivation and desensitization kinetics, pH sensitivity, cation permeability, and binding to allosteric modulators (PubMed:22361591, PubMed:27698419, PubMed:29720657, PubMed:38454578). CHRNB2 forms heteropentameric neuronal acetylcholine receptors with CHRNA2, CHRNA3, CHRNA4 and CHRNA6, as well as CHRNA5 and CHRNB3 as accesory subunits (PubMed:16835356, PubMed:20881005, PubMed:22361591, PubMed:27698419, PubMed:29720657, PubMed:38454578, PubMed:8663494). Found in two major stoichiometric forms,(CHRNA4)3:(CHRNB2)2 and (CHRNA4)2:(CHRNB2)3, the two stoichiometric forms differ in their unitary conductance, calcium permeability, ACh sensitivity and potentiation by divalent cation (PubMed:27698419, PubMed:29720657, PubMed:38454578). Heteropentameric channels with CHRNA6 and CHRNA4 exhibit high sensitivity to ACh and nicotine and are predominantly expressed in only a few brain areas, including dopaminergic neurons, norepirephrine neurons and cells of the visual system. nAChrs containing CHRNA6 subunits mediate endogenous cholinergic modulation of dopamine and gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) release in response to nicotine at nerve terminals (By similarity). Also forms functional nAChRs with other subunits such as CHRNA7:CHRNB2, mainly expressed in basal forebrain cholinergic neurons (PubMed:33239400, PubMed:38161283).CATALYTIC ACTIVITY Ca(2+)(in) = Ca(2+)(out)CATALYTIC ACTIVITY K(+)(in) = K(+)(out)CATALYTIC ACTIVITY Na(+)(in) = Na(+)(out)ACTIVITY REGULATION Activated by a myriad of ligands such as acetylcholine, cytisine, nicotine, choline and epibatidine (PubMed:12527804, PubMed:16835356, PubMed:17132685, PubMed:20881005, PubMed:27698419, PubMed:29720657, PubMed:38454578). Channel potentiation by calcium is stoichiometry-selective, CHRNA4:CHRNB2 nACh receptor is achieved by calcium association with topographically distinct sites framed by anionic residues within the CHRNA4 subunit and between the CHRNA4 and CHRNB2 subunits (PubMed:38454578). Oligomeric amyloid-beta protein 42 activates specifially CHRNA7:CHRNB2 nAchRs (PubMed:33239400). nAChR activity is inhibited by the antagonist alpha-conotoxins BuIA, PnIA, PnIC, GID and MII, small disulfide-constrained peptides from cone snails (PubMed:15609996, PubMed:38161283).SUBUNIT Neuronal AChR is a heteropentamer composed of two different types of subunits: alpha and beta. CHRNB2/Beta-2 subunit can be combined to CHRNA2/alpha-2, CHRNA3/alpha-3 or CHRNA4/alpha-4, CHRNA5/alpha-5, CHRNA6/alpha-6 and CHRNB3/beta-3 to give rise to functional receptors. CHRNA2:CHRNB2 and CHRNA4:CHRNB2 nAChR complexes exist in two subtypes: LS (low agonist sensitivity) with a (CHRNA2/4)3:(CHRNB2)2 and HS (high agonist sensitivity) with a (CHRNA2/4)2:(CHRNB2)3 stoichiometry; the subtypes differ in their subunit binding interfaces which are involved in ligand binding (PubMed:12527804, PubMed:16835356, PubMed:17132685, PubMed:22361591, PubMed:27493220, PubMed:27698419, PubMed:29720657, PubMed:38454578). Cells produce predominantly an (CHRNA4)3:(CHRNB2)2 nAChR. The stoichiometric form (CHRNA4)2:(CHRNB2)3 expression is selectively up-regulated by nicotine and has lower single channel conductance and calcium permeability (PubMed:17132685). Also part of the stoichiometric forms: (CHRNA4:CHRNB2)2:CHRNB3 or (CHRNA6:CHRNB2)2:CHRNB3 (PubMed:16835356). Can form heteropentamers with CHRNA7, mainly found in basal forebrain cholinergic neurons (PubMed:33239400, PubMed:38161283). Interacts with RIC3; which is required for proper folding and assembly (PubMed:16120769). Interacts with LYPD6 (PubMed:27344019).INTERACTION The disease is caused by variants affecting the gene represented in this entry.SIMILARITY Belongs to the ligand-gated ion channel (TC 1.A.9) family. Acetylcholine receptor (TC 1.A.9.1) subfamily. Beta-2/CHRNB2 sub-subfamily.

source_facts.27698419: Human alpha4/beta2 form a heteropentameric pore. Nicotine occupies alpha4(+)/beta2(-) interfaces, with beta2 loopD/E residues contributing. Direct ACh patch-clamp comparison supports both full-length and engineered crystallization constructs. Structure uses intracellular-loop deletions, junction linker and beta2 C-terminal Strep tag; prolonged nicotine produces a desensitized nonconducting structure. Structural state does not negate measured currents.
source_facts.29720657: Both human alpha4beta2 stoichiometries were structurally resolved. The 3alpha:2beta form has an additional alpha-alpha nicotine site; beta2 complementary face and M2 charge composition explain receptor differences. Same large intracellular-loop deletions and tag; calcium-permeability ratio is cited prior physiology, not a new flux measurement in the inspected structural Results.
source_facts.38454578: Human full-length subunit recordings establish ACh-elicited single channels and stoichiometry-selective divalent potentiation. Cryo-EM resolves actual ACh density at alpha4-beta2 and alpha4-alpha interfaces. Structural full-length construct has Bril insertions and tag, alongside loop-deleted constructs. Calcium-site structural/mutational potentiation is not identical to calcium permeation; some sites arise from simulations alone. Alpha4 site mutations are not beta2 calcium-binding-site measurements.
source_facts.38161283: Human alpha7-beta2 concatemer in Xenopus oocytes supports ACh-evoked currents and conotoxin selectivity. Enforced alpha7-beta2-alpha7-beta2-alpha7 stoichiometry plus NACHO; this does not quantify native neuronal stoichiometry/distribution. Alpha6/3 comparator is a chimera. Antagonist allostery does not imply beta2 is an autonomous receptor.
source_facts.24467848: Human alpha2 with beta2 produces agonist currents; codon-optimized beta2 improves expression and was used for subsequent assays. Single-subunit negative controls lack functional receptor. Expression ratios bias putative stoichiometries; exact assembly was not directly counted here. The tested disease-associated variant is alpha2 T22I, not a beta2 mutation.
source_facts.18387948: Human receptor clones expressed in Xenopus yielded baseline ACh responses; mouse Pate-P inhibited human alpha4beta2 net charge. Mixed species of modulator and receptor are explicit. PATE modulation is not proof that CHRNB2 itself is a secreted modulator.
source_facts.20881005: Actual human beta2-alpha4-beta2-alpha4 concatemer plus free alpha5 was tested by voltage clamp and calcium-only currents; the study also tested alpha3beta2alpha5. Full primary resides in preserved CHRNA4 normal/research variant, not the CHRNB2 abstract archive. Alpha5 D398N effect is not transferred to beta2. The reported calcium-only normalization method is retained without claiming an independently calculated permeability coefficient.
source_facts.17132685: Authentic abstract explicitly reports human concatemer-defined receptor stoichiometries, M2 charge mutations and calcium permeability differences. Full Methods not recovered here; use independent full20881005 for inspected calcium-current methodology.
source_facts.15964197: Authentic abstract reports beta2 I312M increases receptor ACh sensitivity. Sensitivity changes alone do not separate binding affinity from gating. Search found request-only author page and limited publisher sections, not full electrophysiology. Underlying beta2 ligand contribution is independently supported by2024 ACh structures.
source_facts.16835356: Authentic abstract explicitly includes human alpha6beta2 and alpha6beta2beta3 assemblies, expression/ligand-binding and cell-system differences. Full current assay protocol not independently accessed; beta3 assembly effects are not assigned as a beta2-specific chaperone function.
source_facts.8906617: Authentic abstract explicitly describes human alpha2/alpha3/alpha4 paired with beta2 or beta4 in oocytes and ACh currents blocked by d-tubocurare. Original full Methods unavailable after the documented access attempts; supports assembled-receptor function, not free beta2 binding.
source_facts.20438829: Selected abstract centers on CHRNA5 ethanol-responsive expression; it does not resolve the background sentence behind beta2 TAS. Do not call wrong-gene miscitation from that abstract. Actual beta2 channel capability is independently secure; exact TAS linkage remains unverified.
source_facts.12189247: Hypoxia and nicotine alter endothelial nicotinic-receptor expression. Beta2-specific changes are reported without displayed data; the angiogenesis pharmacology mainly implicates alpha7.
source_facts.27344019: Recombinant human LYPD6 captures beta2-containing receptors from human cortex, with uncoupled-bead and knockout antibody controls. This is complex association, not purified binary affinity.
source_facts.33961781: Tagged human HEK293T AP-MS records alpha5 and beta2 in the same interaction network. The exact spoke-expanded positive pair supports association without defining native receptor stoichiometry.
source_facts.8663494: The authentic abstract reports human alpha5 coassembly with beta2 in Xenopus oocytes and endogenous alpha5-associated receptors in SH-SY5Y cells; exact curated co-IP records independently preserve those contexts.
source_facts.10531434: Mouse beta2/beta4 loss disrupts autonomic nicotinic signaling and bladder responses, whereas direct muscarinic contraction remains intact. The receptor contribution regulates contraction through the neuronal circuit.
source_facts.15963492: Mouse B-cell nicotinic-receptor experiments include beta2 deletion and context-dependent CD40/nicotine responses. The available abstract does not resolve the precise positive proliferation or activation interpretation.
source_facts.16253349: Mouse knockout/chimera flow cytometry measures lymphocyte population sizes and B-cell precursor survival, including increased annexin-V-positive cells. The accessible abstract does not establish a separately measured B-cell activation assay.
source_facts.11222635: Mouse neuronal recordings connect beta2-containing receptors to acetylcholine currents and depolarization. These experiments are not direct B-cell proliferation measurements.
source_facts.15788760: Beta2-deficient mice have normal young-adult hearing followed by later hearing impairment and spiral-ganglion loss. The result supports auditory neuronal maintenance during aging rather than nerve development.
source_facts.15215293: Beta2-null mice have altered REM-episode duration and stress-induced REM rebound despite similar overall baseline sleep-state amounts.
source_facts.21540349: Lipid perturbations alter currents through rat alpha3/beta2 receptors expressed in hippocampal neurons. The experiments do not distinguish physical receptor redistribution from altered molecular interactions.
source_facts.17559419: Human CHRNB2 variants associate with cognitive-task differences in a female student cohort stratified by smoking history. Association does not identify a directly measured nicotine-induced behavioral change.
source_facts.17900292: A human CHRNB2 V287M variant segregates with familial epilepsy; the clinical pedigree does not establish a separate molecular function.
source_facts.9428762: Mouse beta2 deletion abolishes nicotine-stimulated ventral-striatal dopamine release and neuronal nicotine currents, supporting a receptor-mediated contribution to nicotine responses.
source_facts.10235262: Mouse beta2 loss reduces nicotine antinociception and associated neuronal responses, supporting a contextual nociceptive-circuit contribution.
source_facts.11027228: Mouse beta2 deletion transiently delays refinement of individual retinal ganglion dendrites; initial coarse ON/OFF organization persists and later stratification approaches control patterns.
source_facts.11259617: Rat cortical neurons in long-term primary culture exhibit acetylcholine-evoked currents pharmacologically classified as alpha4/beta2-type and alpha7-type; halothane affects these currents differently. This is native cultured-neuron electrophysiology, not heterologous receptor expression or a direct measurement of pentamer composition.
source_facts.11282258: Beta2-null mice show dose-dependent changes in cocaine place preference and altered dopamine turnover, consistent with an indirect nicotinic influence on reward circuitry.
source_facts.11344259: Loss of mouse beta2-dependent retinal activity disrupts retinofugal organization and visual performance; the receptor supplies activity rather than phototransduction chemistry.
source_facts.12097474: Mouse beta2-null projections develop later local segregation but fail to establish normal eye-specific layers in the lateral geniculate nucleus.
source_facts.12876201: Mouse beta2 loss changes flexible exploration and social behavior without a simple loss of elementary movement.
source_facts.12944511: Mouse receptor immunoprecipitation, dopamine-release assays and neuronal recordings distinguish beta2-containing terminal and somatic receptor populations.
source_facts.12754307: Rat nicotinic-subunit electrophysiology supports cholinergic transmission by assembled beta-containing receptors; the conserved human inference is a receptor contribution.
source_facts.14687550: Mouse beta2-dependent retinal activity contributes to orderly visual projection development. The result does not assign beta2 an autonomous axon-building activity.
source_facts.15016836: Rat heteromeric nicotinic receptors respond to acetylcholine in receptor-expression experiments, supporting the conserved agonist-response capability.
source_facts.15456819: Adult beta2-null visual relay neurons have increased firing; the study leaves developmental and inhibitory-circuit explanations open rather than making the beta2 pore intrinsically inhibitory.
source_facts.15489024: Mouse beta2 loss disrupts nicotine-mediated rescue of ethanol-associated learning effects; alpha7-dependent ethanol sensitivity is a separate result.
source_facts.15541879: An alpha7/beta2 double-mutant mouse experiment links nicotinic receptors to passive avoidance, with the separate contribution of each deleted subunit unresolved.
source_facts.15569257: Mouse alpha4/beta2 receptors stably expressed in human HEK293T cells produce agonist-evoked calcium responses, primarily from entry through the receptor with an additional intracellular-store contribution. This is receptor reconstitution, not an intact-mouse knockout experiment.
source_facts.15608630: Combined beta2 and connexin36 perturbation alters early retinal activity but allows later local segregation, separating distinct activity-dependent stages.
source_facts.16772172: Beta2 deletion and targeted reexpression alter mouse dopamine-neuron firing, linking cholinergic receptor activity to dopaminergic circuit regulation.
source_facts.17301182: Young beta2-null superior-colliculus neurons receive more weak retinal inputs; mature animals have similar input number and strength to controls, indicating developmental refinement.
source_facts.21325521: Rodent electrophysiology distinguishes presynaptic alpha6/beta2-dependent modulation of GABA release from predominantly postsynaptic alpha4/beta2 currents; knockout comparisons and rat recordings have distinct species scopes.

recommendations.reason: The full mouse study locates the nicotinic step in autonomic ganglion neurons. Direct muscarinic contraction remains intact, and electrical stimulation bypasses deficient nicotinic signaling. Beta2/beta4 redundancy supports a regulatory contribution, not absence of beta2 function; the receptor does not perform force generation within smooth muscle.

Preserve both donor branches: IGI PMID15963492 directly studies B cells but its full body was not recovered; IC PMID11222635 establishes neuronal receptor/channel properties and is not direct B-cell proliferation evidence. The available B-cell abstract has context-dependent activation and nicotine responses, so the sign and assay scope cannot be settled. Do not discard the IGI branch because of the separate neural IC source.

Both donor IMP sources really concern mouse lymphocytes. Their unrecovered full bodies are needed to distinguish beta2-dependent activation from precursor survival and population-size effects. Abstract-only access does not justify rejecting experimentally curated evidence or manufacturing a replacement process.

Retain the existing curated circuit-level micturition association on the full mouse IGI study, qualified as autonomic neuronal transmission. The data support beta2/beta4 compensation sustaining acetylcholine delivery to bladder muscle; they do not place beta2 on the final smooth-muscle postsynaptic receptor or directly assay pelvic receptor stoichiometry. This is not a new process claim.
